as_written_in_papers.quote: A hemizygous nonsense mutation (c.35C>A) was identified in the LAMP2 gene of the patient (Figure 4).

cases.statement: One hemizygous male (Patient II / Patient 2, PMID 37609033). PMID 39484323 cites the same patient from that paper (its ref 5, Sun et al); the two batch identities are one person.

people.label: Patient II
people.key_phenotypes: unexplained transaminase elevation from about age 15; dyspnea, weakness and severe exertional fatigue; hepatomegaly with edema; right ventricular hypertrophy with dilated heart and LVEF 23%; extensive late gadolinium enhancement; raised troponin I and CK

quotes.quote: Patient 2 was a 24-year-old male presenting with a distinctly different clinical course and initial manifestation to Patient 1.

The patient was initially referred to a local hospital due to an unexplained elevation of transaminase 9 years ago, 2 years before being referred to the Heart Failure Center, Beijing Anzhen Hospital of Capital Medical University.
Clinical examinations revealed hepatomegaly with obvious edema.
The echocardiographic examination revealed right ventricular hypertrophy (interventricular septum, 13 mm; right ventricle wall, 11 mm) and dilated heart

people.label: ref 5 patient
people.key_phenotypes: right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation; cardiac-only involvement (as summarised from PMID 37609033)

quotes.quote: Sun et al^5 reported a case of a man with right ventricular hypertrophy and dilation with a hemizygous nonsense variant c.35C>A, (pSer12∗) in LAMP2 with DD and only cardiac involvement.
Sun Y.-Q., Lv Q., Chen D., Da Y., Zhao X.-Y., Dong J.-Z. A case study and literature review of the diagnosis of Danon disease in patients presenting only with severe cardiac symptoms.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Cardiac, hepatic and muscle-enzyme findings in a young male. The paper does not say what sequencing method or gene set was used, or whether other causes were excluded.

quotes.quote: For the sequence analysis, DNA was extracted from the blood.
The laboratory results were similar to those of Patient 1 (Table 1).

segregation.statement: No relatives tested. The mother died of DCM in her 40s and a grandfather died at 36 of unexplained causes; no genetic testing was done.

quotes.quote: The patient’s mother died of DCM in her 40s, and their grandfather died at 36 in unexplained circumstances. Nevertheless, no genetic testing was performed.

de_novo.statement: Not tested; the mother was deceased and no relative was tested.

quotes.quote: Nevertheless, no genetic testing was performed.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Nonsense (predicted p.(Ser12Ter)). The authors expect an absent or disrupted protein and say truncating LAMP2 variants are known to cause disease.

quotes.quote: The c.35C>A mutation creates a premature translational stop signal at codon 12 (p.Ser12*) of the LAMP2 gene. It is expected to result in an absent or disrupted protein product.
While this variant has not been reported in the literature, truncating variants in LAMP2 are known to be pathogenic (PMID: 21415759).

population_data_in_papers.statement: Stated absent from ESP, 1000 Genomes and ExAC controls.

quotes.quote: The c.35C>A mutation is absent from controls in the Exome Sequencing Project, the 1000 Genomes Project, and the Exome Aggregation Consortium.

authors_classification.statement: Likely pathogenic under ACMG/AMP 2015 (PMID 37609033; criteria codes not given). PMID 39484323 repeats the citation without its own classification.

quotes.quote: Based on this evidence, this mutation has been classified as likely pathogenic according to ACMG/AMP 2015 guidelines.^6

concerns: Same person twice: DANON-ID0497 (PMID 39484323, 'ref 5 patient') is a literature citation of DANON-ID0252 (PMID 37609033, Patient II); reference 5 of PMID 39484323 is PMID 37609033. Count once.

PMID 37609033 gives a genomic coordinate (chrX-119602990), apparently GRCh37 by analogy with Patient I's stated GRCh37 coordinate; the build is not stated for Patient II. No transcript stated for this variant (Patient I's is NM_002294.2).

PMID 37609033 labels the person both 'Patient 2' and 'Patient II', and has an incomplete sentence on family history ('Only the relatives on the mother’s side of the family.'). The grandfather's side is not stated.
PMID 37609033's title says 'presenting only with severe cardiac symptoms', but Patient II also had hepatomegaly, transaminase elevation and weakness.
notes_for_panel: One hemizygous male with a nonsense variant near the start of the protein and a maternal history of early cardiac death; no relatives tested; sequencing method not described.
